**1.3 Steering System Choices**

**1.3.1 Steering Motor Selection**

* We selected the LEGO EV3 Medium Servo Motor (45503) to operate our steering mechanism. It is vertically mounted to drive the steering linkage through LEGO Part 33299\.  
* The Medium Motor was chosen because of its compact size, sufficient torque for operating the steering mechanism, and responsive movement. 

**1.3.2 Steering Structure**

**![][image2]**

Our steering system combines LEGO Part 33299 with fully custom-designed 3D-printed components. Using LEGO axles and connectors, all components are assembled into a complete steering mechanism, ensuring proper alignment and coordinated movement of both front wheels.

**1.3.3 Ackermann Steering Geometry**  
**![][image9]**

* Our steering system follows the Ackermann steering principle, where the inner front wheel turns at a greater angle than the outer front wheel.  
* As shown in our robot chassis, the steering linkages control both front wheels at different angles during cornering.   
* The projected wheel axes meet at a common Instantaneous Centre of Rotation (ICR), allowing the wheels to follow a different turning radius.

* This reduces tyre scrubbing, minimizes unnecessary friction and improves the robot's turning efficiency and maneuverability.

**Using our robot chassis as an example:**

1\. **Inner Wheel (${\alpha }_{i}$)** – During a left turn, the left front wheel is the inner wheel. It turns at a larger angle because it follows a smaller turning radius.

2\. **Outer Wheel (${\alpha }_{o}$))** – The right front wheel is the outer wheel. It turns at a smaller angle because it follows a larger turning radius.

3\. **Centre Steering Angle (${\alpha }_{c}$))** – Represents the reference steering angle at the centre of the front axle, between the inner and outer wheel angles.

4\. **Instantaneous Centre of Rotation (ICR)** – The projected lines perpendicular to the direction of each wheel meet at a common point called the ICR. This allows all four wheels to follow their respective turning paths without unnecessary sideways slipping.

**1.3.4 Ackermann Steering Testing and Calculation**

| ![][image10] | ![][image11] |
| ----- | :---: |
| $\cot {\alpha }_{o}-\cot {\alpha }_{i}=\frac{B}{L}$  $\cot {\alpha }_{o}-\cot 3{5}^{\circ }=\frac{95}{125}$  $\cot {\alpha }_{o}=1.4281+0.76$  $\cot {\alpha }_{o}=2.1881$  ${\alpha }_{o}={\tan }^{-1}\left({\frac{1}{2.1881}}\right)$                              ${\alpha }_{o}=$ 24.57°  |  |

* During a left turn, the left front wheel turns at a larger angle of 35°, while the right front wheel turns at a smaller angle of 24.57°.  
* This helps both front wheels follow their respective turning paths and provides smoother cornering.   
  


**1.3.5 Steering System Trade-off and Engineering Decisions**

| Advantages of Ackermann Steering System | Disadvantages of Ackermann Steering System |
| :---: | :---: |
| Better turning performance | Complex linkage design |
| Reduced tyre scrubbing | Additional components |
| Improve Manoeuvrability | Assembly effort |

* The Ackermann steering system was selected because it provides better turning performance, reduces tyre scrubbing and improves manoeuvrability.   
* Although it requires a more complex linkage design and additional assembly effort, its steering benefits outweigh these disadvantages. 

**Previous vs New Steering System:**

| Aspect | Previous Steering System | New Steering System |
| :---: | ----- | :---: |
| **Picture** | ![][image12] | ![][image13] |
| **Steering Structure** | Two equal-length linkages | Ackermann steering linkage |
| **Wheel Angle** | Both front wheels turn at approximately the same angle | Inner wheel turns at a greater angle |
| **Tyre Scrubbing** | More likely during cornering | Reduced tyre scrubbing |
| **Mechanical Complexity** | Simple structure | More complex linkage design |

* Despite the increased mechanical complexity and assembly effort, we selected the Ackermann steering system for its improved steering accuracy, reduced tyre scrubbing and smoother cornering.   
* Overall, the performance benefits outweigh the additional design complexity, making it a better choice for our competition robot.
